node_7.description: Nagi regards the drive to excel as most meaningful when it lifts a group rather than distinguishes an individual â€” competitive striving is legitimate and admirable, but personal glory at the group's expense is not.

node_10.description: Nagi regards ambiguity and improvisation as sources of genuine discomfort â€” clarity about what is expected and how things will proceed allows one to act with confidence and full commitment.

node_11.description: Nagi holds that one's efforts and conduct matter beyond their immediate outcomes â€” the value of what a person does extends into a future they may not personally see, and this gives everyday actions a weight that short-term results alone cannot capture.

node_13.description: Nagi regards adaptation to circumstances as entirely compatible with integrity â€” adjusting one's approach as conditions change is pragmatic wisdom, not inconsistency.
